title: Deep transfer learning detects methane super-emitters in oil and gas fields from Sentinel-2
summary: A two-part framework (adaptive artifact removal plus a deep subdomain adaptation network) was trained on 1,627 Sentinel-2 images from six known methane super-emitters. Applied to an unannotated oil field in Algeria, it flagged 34 anomalous emission events over one year, attributed to three super-emitters linked to production and transmission infrastructure. DSAN achieved an average macro F1 of 0.86 on transfer tasks, versus 0.78 for the EfficientNet-V2L comparator; independent field verification is not reported in the abstract.
ai_technology: Deep subdomain adaptation network (DSAN) with low-reflectance artifact detection (LRAD)
organization: Westlake University; Zhejiang University; Harvard University
